Bloomberg today published the latest report, providing an in-depth analysis of Apple's Mac product line planning. The report details the update plans for several products including MacBook Pro, MacBook Air, and iMac over the coming years.

Brand new MacBook Air, iMac, MacBook Pro, and other new machines

Bloomberg pointed out that Apple aims to launch the following new Macs before the end of this year:

  • New entry-level MacBook Pro equipped with M6 chip
  • Brand new iMac
  • New high-end 14-inch and 16-inch touchscreen MacBook series equipped with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips with OLED displays

The report stated that this batch of new high-end MacBook models is "scheduled to launch between the end of this year and early next year as planned." Apple is testing with macOS 27.1, which is expected to be released at the end of October.

Apple plans to launch an updated MacBook Air series in early 2027. The company is also developing a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro equipped with the M7 chip, expected to debut next year.

A new MacBook Neo is also under development, with Apple testing models equipped with the A19 Pro chip. The report indicated that Apple also plans to "regularly" release new colour options for the MacBook Neo.

Apple is also testing Mac mini models equipped with M5 Pro and basic M6 processors. Meanwhile, several new Mac Studio models with M5 Max and M5 Ultra processors are also being tested. Bloomberg reminded: "However, the launch timing of these machines, as well as the planned chip and memory configurations, will depend on memory chip supply."

Looking further ahead, Bloomberg reported that an OLED version of the MacBook Air is under development and could debut as early as "2028." According to reports, Apple is also developing an OLED version of the iMac, which will follow the OLED MacBook Air.

What are your thoughts on Apple's rumoured Mac product roadmap? Are you planning to upgrade in the near future? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
